subject: Q2 renewal — graduated uplift ladder, billing cutover & co-term plan
content:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal / mid-contract expansion — Q2 uplift ask

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. We expect another major feature rollout in late Q2 and need to lock in additional reserved capacity for inference (approx 1.2B tokens/month incremental, peak burst to 2.5B).

Before I engage procurement, can you confirm:
- An uplift path that preserves our current co-term to 2028-01-31
- How proration will be handled mid-billing-cycle (we're currently monthly)
- Whether there are blended discount tiers if we commit to a stepped annualized uplift vs. a single top-up?

I've attached our Q1 usage report and the SOW draft for context. Procurement also asked about any exec approval required for pricing beyond the baseline.

Thanks,
Sarah Liu
Head of Product
Acme Robotics

---------- Original message headers and attachments ----------
Attachments: usage_report_Q1.csv, Acme_SOW_v3.pdf

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal / mid-contract expansion — Q2 uplift ask

Hi Sarah — great to hear about the rollout, congrats.

Short answers up front:
- We can co-term the uplift with your existing renewal date (2028-01-31); we'll treat the uplift as an amendment that lives under the same contract.
- Proration: for monthly billing we do a pro-rata invoice for the remainder of the current month + then the new monthly rate thereafter. If you annualize the uplift we can provide an annualized blended price and adjust billing cadence (and credit for months remaining).
- Discount tiers: yes — we support a graduated (stair-step) discount ladder that gives better unit pricing as committed monthly throughput increases; we can also offer a staged incentive if you sign an annualized uplift (3% additional discount at 12-month commit, for example).

I'll loop in Ben from sales to put together a concise options matrix (looks like he already has some draft pricing). Is procurement ok with a one-off amendment + new PO? If they prefer an addendum and new SOW flow we can accommodate it.

Best,
Olga
Director, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

---------- Forwarded internal planning thread ----------
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal / mid-contract expansion — Q2 uplift ask

Team — forwarding Acme's ask. Need a tight playbook we can present to procurement: 1) staged uplift ladder with blended pricing; 2) co-term approach and cutover dates; 3) billing/proration mechanics; 4) optional early-pay term to unlock extra discount.

Ben — can you draft the pricing matrix for the three scenarios below?
- Scenario A (Short spike): 6 months incremental commitment, monthly billing, modest 7% uplift discount on incremental usage.
- Scenario B (Stair-step): staged 3-bucket commit over 12 months (months 1–4: +40% capacity, months 5–8: +80%, months 9–12: +120%) with laddered unit price improvements at each jump.
- Scenario C (Annualize now): Annualized additional commit (12 months) with a blended rate and 3% early-pay discount option.

Marcus — need your input on runtime capacity guarantees and whether we should recommend Dedicated burst buffer for the Q2 launch (affects pricing and SLA).

Naomi — ops/billing: what's the cleanest invoice / credit approach so procurement doesn't have to do month-by-month reconciliation? Could we issue a single pro-rated invoice then set the new recurring amount?

Thanks,
Olga

---
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal / mid-contract expansion — Q2 uplift ask

Thanks Olga — draft matrix attached (redwood_pricing_matrix.xlsx). High-level guidance: we should present Scenario B as the recommended commercial — it balances lower initial spend for Acme while giving them predictable tiers they can opt into. Proposed concrete numbers in the attachment; summary below:
- Base uplift (incremental tokens): 1.2B/mo baseline as requested.
- Ladder discounts: Tier1 (+40%) => $0.XX/token (7% off), Tier2 (+80%) => $0.XX/token (12% off), Tier3 (+120%) => $0.XX/token (18% off).
- Annualize option: blended per-token price ~ 5% lower than highest tier, plus a 3% early-pay if they commit to annual billing and up-front payment.

For co-term, recommend we:
1) Amend contract effective upon DocuSign signature with start date = first day of next billing cycle after signature.
2) Pro-rate the remainder of the current month; issue a single pro-rated invoice.
3) Set the new monthly recurring based on the chosen scenario and apply billed credits if annualization occurs mid-month.

I'll prepare a clean one-pager for procurement and a redlined SOW example.

Ben
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal / mid-contract expansion — Q2 uplift ask

Olga / team — technical considerations:
- If Acme expects sustained peaks at ~2.5B tokens during rollout, we should recommend a Dedicated burst pool for the launch window (30–45 days) to guarantee tail latencies and avoid throttling. That would be priced as a short-term reserved buffer (one-time monthly equivalent).
- KV cache and prefix caching policies will greatly reduce effective token costs for repeated calls — include a note in the one-pager about expected effective unit reduction (15–25%) if they adopt our recommended cache settings.
- SLA: for any Dedicated buffer we recommend including a short-term SLA addendum (72-hour remediation for capacity failures) given the higher financial commitment.

I'll include an estimated incremental cost for Dedicated buffer in the one-pager.

Marcus
Head of Runtime Ops

---
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal / mid-contract expansion — Q2 uplift ask

Billing flow we can commit to:
- Issue a single pro-rata invoice for the remainder of current month upon signed amendment.
- Start new monthly recurring charges on the first day of next billing cycle.
- If customer annualizes mid-cycle and pays up-front, we issue credit equal to months remaining toward the annualized price and carry it as a prepaid balance applied to future invoices (clean for procurement).
- For staged ladder (Scenario B) we can automate tier ramping and generate a quarterly reconciliation report so they don't need to manually track month-to-month.

Attachments: sample invoice template (we'll include in the one-pager).

Naomi
Revenue Ops

---
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal / mid-contract expansion — Q2 uplift ask

Thanks — this is helpful. Procurement confirmed they prefer Scenario B (stair-step) with the Dedicated burst buffer for the first 45 days of the rollout. Their asks:
- A finalized one-pager with explicit numbers for the three ladder tiers and the Dedicated buffer price.
- A clear DocuSign amendment that preserves the 2028-01-31 co-term.
- Procurement will require the pro-rated invoice and SOW to be attached to the DocuSign package.

Can you send the one-pager and amended SOW by EOD Monday? Procurement wants to start the review cycle Tues morning.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to hop on a 30-min sync if useful.

Best,
Sarah

Attachments referenced: Acme_SOW_v3.pdf (from earlier), usage_report_Q1.csv

---
Notes for Olga's mailbox: next steps — Ben to finalize pricing one-pager + attach redwood_pricing_matrix.xlsx; Marcus to provide Dedicated buffer cost line; Naomi to attach sample invoice and SOW redline. Prepare DocuSign package with the amendment + SOW + invoice.
